pcs.pc_description: List all refrigeration equipment, record their key specifications and tag critical systems.
Review OEM Guidelines, Maintenance Manuals and manufacturer manuals for each unit.
Identify the recommended service intervals, Parts replacement timelines, Calibration/ inspection points, and Critical thresholds for temperature, pressure, and performance.

Prepare work program and schedules for maintenance based on equipment criticality (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annually), Usage intensity (24/7 operation vs. seasonal use) and Environment (high-dust, high-humidity, or food- grade zones).
Prioritize maintenance as per legislative laws, organisation requirements, resources, and environment
Plan electrical system maintenance at least once in five years as per the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Code of Practice

Develop PM Checklists for Each Equipment Type which should include Visual Inspection (corrosion, leaks, frost buildup), Mechanical Check (compressor noise, vibration, fan operation), Electrical Check (connections, insulation, relays, overloads), Refrigerant System Check (leak detection, pressure testing, level verification), Cleaning Tasks (coils, filters, panels, drain lines) and Control System Calibration (thermostats, sensors, defrost timers, BMS/PLC inputs).
Be sure electrical connections for corroded terminals, evaporators for defrosting, and coil surfaces for dust accumulation checks are included.
Confirm that the maintenance plan checks oil safety and high-pressure controls of compressor units
Schedule PM during non-peak hours or planned downtime, and coordinate with production, warehouse, or logistics teams to minimise disruption.
Record the schedules for preventive maintenance and share them with the respective stakeholders.
Identify resources for maintenance based on the skills required and timelines.
Assign roles and responsibilities to those who perform which tasks, such as an in-house technician vs. an external service contractor.
Provide information on priority to the mechanics and deadlines for the tasks, so that losses are minimized
Make contingency plans for emergencies regarding the working of the equipment and for variations in workforce availability.

pcs.pc_description: Inspect regularly to ensure maintenance activities are done as per quality requirements, timelines and within the costs planned.
Prepare preventive maintenance Calendar and Monitor the sequence of activities as per the schedule and that the equipment is calibrated correctly before use.
Ensure compliance with Refrigerant handling regulations (e.g., India’s Ozone Depleting Substances Rules) and Electrical safety and lockout/tagout procedures.
Confirm that the quality of the products stored under refrigeration is not harmed while equipment components are being checked
Ensure that there is safe discharge of ammonia, so that excess refrigerant is discharged safely (not inside the cold room and away from the work area)
Ensure that drains in the cold area are free of debris and check the operations of door seals.
Ensure workers are using PPE and leave the area safe and clean after performing maintenance activities
Carry out a walk-around inspection regularly to monitor the activities of subordinates.
Allocate parallel tasks to handle different components of refrigeration equipment, like the evaporator, compressor and condenser, wherever possible
Observe the work efficiency of the workforce and identify training needs wherever necessary
Communicate with workers as often as needed to ensure the maintenance schedule is followed
Do warranty analysis and tag critical systems.
Renew license with concerned authorities every year as per the AMC Expiry of certain equipments.
Assign a resource to maintain records during refrigeration equipment maintenance activities
Conduct regular checks on the maintenance log and instruct the person concerned if it’s inaccurate.
Maintain logs for the Maintenance performed, Spare parts used, Issues found and resolved, Equipment downtime and repair history, etc.
Use CMMS (Computerised Maintenance Management System) or digital tools like Excel, UpKeep, or Maintainx.
Review failure logs and service history every 6 months and update maintenance schedules based on Unexpected breakdowns, Equipment age or upgrade, Energy efficiency targets, etc.
Incorporate feedback from operators and facility managers and maintain the Operational Calendar.

Log all installation/replacement steps, parameters, and refrigerant weight used.
Update asset tag, service record, and maintenance database.
Provide commissioning report, warranty documents, and system manual to facility management.
Monitor performance trends of the equipment and check operator feedback.

pcs.pc_description: Carry out tests or checks regularly to ensure the system is working as required
Check for freezer insulation degradation by observing compressor duty cycle, condensation or presence of ice
Check the operation of the defrost system and thermostat and ensure that the equipment is calibrated correctly before using it.
Inspect cold store ceiling panel suspension rods and also their attachments at least once a year
Examine discharge pressure and suction pressure in the control system and make adjustments if necessary
Ensure that hygiene procedures are followed
Physically inspect systems for Unusual noises, vibrations, leaks, or icing and Audit refrigerant levels and compressor efficiency

Test the working of the equipment, after service or repair and Compare actual vs. expected performance.
Plan repairs limited to thermostats, electrical systems, start relays and defrost timers as much as possible
Avoid repairs to the cooling system if they are uneconomical, and consider replacement of components.

Define Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Establish measurable benchmarks to assess equipment performance such as Temperature stability (vs. setpoint), Compressor run time and cycling frequency, Energy consumption (kWh per unit or per hour), Refrigerant pressure and level, Frequency of breakdowns or maintenance calls, Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF), Mean Time to Repair (MTTR), etc.
Set Up Real-Time Monitoring Tools and Install sensors and data loggers to track Temperature, humidity, pressure, and power usage.
Collect and Analyse Data Regularly to review equipment data daily/weekly for trends and anomalies.
Collect and Analyse Data Regularly to review equipment data daily/weekly for trends and anomalies.

Implement Corrective & Preventive Actions such as Adjust setpoints or defrost cycles for energy optimization, Replace underperforming components (e.g., fans, motors, valves), Upgrade to energy-efficient parts or automation systems, etc.
Revise maintenance schedules (move from time-based to condition-based where possible).

Maintain a Continuous Improvement Log containing Identified issues, Corrective actions, Outcomes (energy saved, fewer breakdowns, better temperature control) and Use this to justify investments or schedule capital upgrades.
Maintain issue logs and complaints by Internal ticketing management of issues like regular ticket, unexpected ticket and renewal ticket.
Train maintenance staff to follow safety procedures while handling refrigerants and provide information on hazardous effects of refrigerants to the environment.

Teach maintenance staff on procedures while removing or replacing an evaporator, condenser or compressor.
Sensitize maintenance staff on the energy consumption of refrigeration equipment and ways to conserve energy.
Train maintenance staff to recognise early signs of failure, promptly report anomalies, and follow updated SOPs.
Instruct staff to inspect, dismantle, repair, and reinstate refrigeration components (evaporators, condensers, compressors) using appropriate tools, techniques, and control circuit diagrams.
Guide staff to perform required numerical calculations, data entry, and support improvement of feedback loops.
Train staff on emergency responses for malfunctioning refrigeration equipment or components.
Educate staff on FSSAI hygiene, temperature, and documentation compliance for cold chain operations.
